evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep opens with 'we just do a quick twenty minute or so virtual walkthrough' but never delivers the standard framing (time-boxed ask + promise of dependable quote + waiting for yes). Customer immediately raises a constraint (meeting at 4pm), rep pivots to phone estimate instead without the quid pro quo.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Rep asked about 'the kind of move' and 'total gym' details but never explicitly asked for: customer name (uses 'Mike' but unclear if that's confirmation), moving date (only mentioned Oct 11 at the end), city-to-city route, or approximate square footage. Only 2–3 of the four basics covered.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Customer states he's moving 'prepacked boxes,' 'furniture,' and 'potted plants' — no explicit square footage given, but rep never offered the virtual walkthrough option after pivoting to phone estimate. Rep should have assessed home size and offered the walkthrough per script Section 1.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' Rep immediately probed for specific items (gym equipment, plants) without eliciting the customer's underlying concerns or agenda.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer never raised any concerns beyond logistics. Rep asked about gym equipment specs and plant size, but these were logistics probes, not concerns.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised, so no reflection needed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covered: special items (gym equipment, potted plants, trees), but missed or didn't clearly establish: property type, floor/stories, number of rooms, walking distance, additional rooms (only mentioned 'boxes' but not room count), additional stops. About 3–4 of 7 items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep asked 'boxes wise typically a home this size prepacked boxes' but did NOT offer packing services. Customer volunteered he's packing himself. Rep did not ask the standard 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — false.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep stated 'typically a home this size prepacked boxes, where you're usually seeing around eighty or ninety. Do you think that sounds fair or you think you have more?' — true, though customer clarified he's packing his own boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave both range and personalization: 'for a move like this... I would do a two truck and foreman crew. Our hourly rate is $384... typical range of cost is between $1,920 and $2,688. We are most efficient with big furniture impact boxes. The loose miscellaneous items tend to add the most time.' — full.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: hourly rate ($96 per guy), 2.5 hour minimum ($960), 15-minute increments, all-inclusive (zero additional fees, pads, wrap, disassemble, reassembly, TV bag, door protection, floor runners, insurance, no credit card fees or taxes). Missing: trip fee or overnight fee transparency (not mentioned as applicable). Full disclosure of what IS included and the minimum framing — full.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Customer says 'Yeah, I think so' in response to 'Does that all kind of make sense?' but that's answering about the 2.5 hour minimum mechanics, not pricing fairness. Rep did not pause after pricing — not asked.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'we do have on time guarantees if we're ever late to a window. We give you we do discount your money back.' — covers the discount-immediately framing but phrasing is slightly unclear. Recognizable version present — full.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'in our rate is our no worries, damage coverage. It's just higher evaluation that we provide. There's no charge for that. It allocates up to $2,000 per move... if anything happened we cover that stuff.' — covers the $2,000, no deductible/no-fine-print framing ('there's no charge,' 'goes well above and beyond'), and that it's built in. Full.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Rep moved directly to availability and booking without confirming the two promises resolved customer concerns. No closing-the-loop question — false.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or 'Any other concerns?' After pricing, rep moved straight to 'So currently, we do have the two trucks and four guys available' without a final concerns check — not asked.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep asked 'And then any other thing else like a beef for a piano or antiques. Anything else that we have that we should know about in advance.' — asked during probing (Section 3), not during the final concerns check (Section 6). No catch-all in Section 6 — false.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Customer volunteered 'we have might as well get it on the calendar' in response to rep saying 'So currently, we do have the two trucks and four guys available for Sunday October 11th.' Rep presented availability but never explicitly asked for the business — never.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep mentioned 'no rescheduling or cancellation fees' but did NOT mention rate-lock or rate guarantee. Customer is not locked into the quoted price — false.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed: date (Sunday October 11th), email address (OU Griff @gmail.com). Missing or partial: phone number (not confirmed), arrival window (not specified), crew size (mentioned '2 trucks and 4 guys' but not confirmed in booking), addresses (rep said it will be 'in the confirmation' but did not read back or confirm), notes for crew about customer concerns (rep did not document or mention what the customer was worried about). Partial confirmation — 2 of 6 items fully confirmed on the call.

top_strength: Calvin clearly explained pricing mechanics (hourly rate, minimum, increments, all-inclusive coverage) and delivered both the On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage promises fully and credibly.
coaching_note: Calvin never asked the customer's concerns or agenda (Section 2) and skipped the critical 'Does that feel fair?' pause after pricing (Section 4), jumping straight to availability — these two gaps collapsed discovery and left money on the table before the ask, which was also never made explicitly.
